messages.subject: Trouble with brain registrations when using xform_brain
messages.subject_clean: Trouble with brain registrations when using xform_brain
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

First of all many thanks Dr Jefferis for this brilliant tool. It's unlocked a lot of exciting avenues for research :)

I am having some issues using the xform_brain function. When trying to transform a neuron of interest to a new brain registration:

object_487623337 <- neuprint_read_neurons(487623337)
plot3d(object_487623337)
object_487623337_JRC2018F <- xform_brain(object_487623337*8/1000, reference=JRC2018F, sample="JRCFIB2018F")

I get this error as output:
Transforming neurons using the sequence: JRCFIB2018F->JRC2018F
Error in H5File.open(filename, mode, file_create_pl, file_access_pl) :
  HDF5-API Errors:
    error #000: c:/msys64/home/Jeroen/hdf5-1.8.16/src/H5F.c in H5Fopen(): line 604: unable to open file
        class: HDF5
        major: File accessibilty
        minor: Unable to open file

    error #001: c:/msys64/home/Jeroen/hdf5-1.8.16/src/H5Fint.c in H5F_open(): line 1087: unable to read superblock
        class: HDF5
        major: File accessibilty
        minor: Read failed

    error #002: c:/msys64/home/Jeroen/hdf5-1.8.16/src/H5Fsuper.c in H5F_super_read(): line 294: unable to load superblock
        class: HDF5
        major: Object cache
        minor: Unable to protect metadata

    error #003: c:/msys64/home/Jeroen/hdf5-1.8.16/src/H5AC.c in H5AC_protect(): line 1262: H5C_protect() failed.
        class: HDF5
        major: Object cache
        minor: Unable to protect metadata

    error #004: c:/msys64/home/Jeroen/hdf5-1.8.16/src/H5C.c in H5C_protect(): line 3574: can't load entry
        class: HDF5
        major: Object cache
        minor

This is confusing because the file path mentioned in the error message doesn't exist on my computer, despite me having a genuine path to these files. Do you know how I might pass the correct file path to the xform_brain function? I would be very grateful for any guidance.

Best,
Rory

messages.subject_clean: [nat-user] Trouble with brain registrations when using xform_brain
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rory, glad these tools are proving useful and sorry you’re having trouble. It does look like you have a problem with HDF5 access. The paths relate to the source code when compiled, likely on Jeroen Oom's computer. I would think these are plausible diagnoses to exclude:

1. the Bogovic/Saalfeld h5 registrations are missing
2. They are corrupt
3. your h5 library/dependencies are not properly installed

To check 1 can you do:

nat.jrcbrains:::list_saalfeldlab_registrations()

It might be good to do:

nat.templatebrains::allreg_dataframe()

as well.

To check 2 and 3, can you do:

nat.h5reg::dr_h5reg()

and report back on what it says.

It is probably also worth running

natverse::natverse_update()

All the best,

Greg.

Sent from my iPhone

Dear Greg,

Thanks for getting back to me so soon and spending the time to help me. I had installed the registrations, and their file paths appear when I use nat.jrcbrains:::list_saalfeldlab_registrations().

I couldn't initially get nat.h5reg::dr_h5reg() to work as it seemed there was an issue with rJava. I fixed this by installing the right version etc, so now when using nat.h5reg::dr_h5reg() again, things seem to be working ok as I get this message:
rJava
----
The rJava package is linked to the following JVM
java.version: 1.8.0_271
java.home: C:\Program Files\Java\jre1.8.0_271
java.class.version: 52.0

System java
----
(used as a fallback when rJava not available)
No java command line tool found in your path!

h5reg test
----
h5reg xform infrastructure OK!
xform test gave correct results

However unfortunately now I have a new issue when trying to use xform_brains as before:
object_487623337_JRC2018F <- xform_brain(object_487623337*8/1000, reference=JRC2018F, sample="JRCFIB2018F"):

Transforming neurons using the sequence: JRCFIB2018F->JRC2018F

Error in .jcall("RJavaTools", "Ljava/lang/Object;", "invokeMethod", cl,  :
"]ncsa.hdf.hdf5lib.exceptions.HDF5FileInterfaceException: File accessibilty:File has been truncated ["..\..\src\H5Fsuper_cache.c line 476 in H5F_sblock_load(): truncated file: eof = 331485184, sblock->base_addr = 0, stored_eoa = 1289362629

It does seem like maybe there's an issue with the registration files. Is it worth just deleting these and trying to install them again?

Best,
Rory

Dear Rory,

It looks like some/all of your h5 format registration files were not correctly downloaded. You could see if they are intact by comparing the md5 hash values like so:

> tools::md5sum(dir(nat.jrcbrains:::list_saalfeldlab_registrations(), full.names = T))
              /Users/jefferis/Library/Application Support/R/nat.jrcbrains/JRC2018F_FAFB/JRC2018F_FAFB.h5
                                                                      "957a49cfb878a40f2cb1931147b2f792"
              /Users/jefferis/Library/Application Support/R/nat.jrcbrains/JRC2018F_FCWB/JRC2018F_FCWB.h5
                                                                      "e154d1ac8b144b98558bdeb5f948143e"
      /Users/jefferis/Library/Application Support/R/nat.jrcbrains/JRC2018F_JFRC2010/JRC2018F_JFRC2010.h5
                                                                      "129563e7f6e8a4febdfc50fcda63d0ee"
      /Users/jefferis/Library/Application Support/R/nat.jrcbrains/JRC2018F_JFRC2013/JRC2018F_JFRC2013.h5
                                                                      "4e756f8217cb564b5e3f4000586f4b2b"
/Users/jefferis/Library/Application Support/R/nat.jrcbrains/JRC2018F_JRCFIB2018F/JRC2018F_JRCFIB2018F.h5
                                                                      "a06b11c11dfe1e830209d40893f6d586"
      /Users/jefferis/Library/Application Support/R/nat.jrcbrains/JRC2018U_JRC2018F/JRC2018U_JRC2018F.h5
                                                                      "d292eccfa8ec323f0d98c3e2dddff3af"

I'm afraid the download is not clever, so it will download everything from scratch even if the file already exists when you do:

nat.jrcbrains::download_saalfeldlab_registrations()

Re rJava, that is optional but should be an improvement. Did nat.h5reg::dr_h5reg() fail for you before that was fixed. Of course the intention is that it should still run and warn you about the problem.

All the best,

Greg.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Greg I hope you are well.

I am trying to install natverse using the following in R studio:

install.packages("natmanager") natmanager::install('natverse')

I get the following error:

Error: `github_token()` was deprecated in usethis 2.0.0 and is now defunct.
Call `gh::gh_token()` to retrieve a GitHub personal access token
Call `gh_token_help()` if you need help getting or configuring your token

I already have the token in the Renviron.

I would really appreciate it if you could help me.

Best Regards
Ibrahim

messages.subject: Re: problem with installing natverse
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ibrahim, this is due to an incompatible change in one of the dependencies, the usethis package. We have an issue already

https://github.com/natverse/natmanager/issues/15

and Sri is working on a fix which I expect will be ready tomorrow. If you need to to get round this in the meantime, you can roll usethis back to version 2.0 using remotes::install_github.

All the best,

Greg.

Sent from my iPhone

Dear Greg,

Thanks for your suggestions in trying to solve the issue. Unfortunately despite downloading the saalfeld lab registrations again, and also trying reinstalling a few of the natverse packages, the same issue remains: while some of the registration files have hash values matching the ones you posted above, some repeatedly have incorrect hash values (including the ones I am trying to use). Do you know of any reason that might explain some of the files being downloaded correctly, while others aren't? Could there be a particular natverse package which might be part of the issue? Sorry to keep bothering you with this, I appreciate your cooperation so far.

One thing to note is that when I use nat.jrcbrains::download_saalfeldlab_registrations(), I get a strange progress readout during download, like this:
[1073741824%] Downloaded 0 bytes....
Where the downloaded bytes stays at 0 while the % moves through a set of random numbers. I wonder if this could be something to do with it?

Best,
Rory

Dear Greg,

Great, this led to a solution! With file.info <http://file.info>() I noticed that some of the files were much smaller than they should have been, and in the end I downloaded them manually through figshare links I found online and put these files into the correct directories. This then led to the xform_brain function working correctly on my neurons of interest. Still not quite sure why it didn't work correctly through R, but for now this will allow me to advance with my project. Thanks a lot for your help in trouble shooting this.

Rory
